neighbours.label: ' to' / '-to' in the phrase 'up to' (up to 60%, up to now, up-to-date)
fire: Shoppers can save up to 40 percent on winter coats this week.
The new battery lasts up to twelve hours on a single charge.
Our records are kept up-to-date by a small team of volunteers.
The stadium holds up to fifty thousand fans on match days.
Until last year, and up to that moment, nobody had noticed the leak.
Each guest may bring up to two bags on the shuttle bus.
Make sure your antivirus software is up to date before you browse.
The fine for littering can reach up to five hundred dollars.
quiet: Shoppers can save almost 40 percent on winter coats this week.
The new battery lasts about twelve hours on a single charge.
Our records are maintained by a small team of volunteers.
The stadium holds nearly fifty thousand fans on match days.
Until last year, nobody had noticed the leak in the roof.
Each guest may bring two bags on the shuttle bus to the hotel.
Make sure you install the latest antivirus software before you browse.
The fine for littering can reach five hundred dollars in the city.

notes: Card: ' to' x26 and '-to' x6, every top example is 'up to' or 'up-to-date'. Near misses keep 'to' or 'up' but not the bigram.
